levers.name: Core digital team
levers.description: A core of skilled staff who lead products, oversee vendors, and act as an informed buyer; includes fellowships, hiring reform, upskilling, and product operating model. It does not by itself take over vendor work; that is the insourcing lever.

levers.name: In-house delivery at scale (insourcing)
levers.description: Growing in-house staff to build and run work vendors do now. Programme overhead only; salaries are charged separately by the engine in proportion to in-house staff capacity.

levers.name: Spend controls and service standards
levers.description: A central body that can approve or block spending and set service standards.

levers.name: Legal mandate (legislation)
levers.description: Digital duties and institutions written into law through legislation. Costs little to run but takes heavy political effort to pass (see EFFORT).

levers.name: Product (continuous) funding
levers.description: Stable annual funding for teams and services, including central modernization funds.

levers.name: Policy and process simplification
levers.description: Simpler rules and fewer procedural barriers, with implementers involved in writing policy.

levers.name: Strategic and modular procurement
levers.description: Using awards and renewals for leverage, and splitting contracts into replaceable pieces.

levers.name: Data rights and open interfaces
levers.description: Government ownership of data and documentation, open APIs, and interoperability mandates.

levers.name: New-entrant and mission-aligned vendor pipeline
levers.description: Marketplaces, challenge-based buying, startup pipelines, and public-benefit vendors.

levers.name: Funding open source maintenance
levers.description: Paying for upkeep of the code public services depend on.

levers.name: Shared platforms (DPI building blocks)
levers.description: Common identity, payments, notifications, and data exchange, including digital public goods.

levers.name: Collaboration between governments
levers.description: Jointly owned infrastructure, consortia, peer networks, and cooperative purchasing.

levers.name: Accountability and safeguards
levers.description: Algorithm registers, impact assessments, accessibility, redress, and open contracting.

levers.name: Public option
levers.description: Government builds and runs the service or infrastructure itself.

not_modeled.H2: Competition enforcement is usually outside the control of the jurisdiction delivering services.
not_modeled.I4: Civil society and civic tech capacity is external and hard to represent as a government choice.

relationships.framework_row: In-house talent -> strategic procurement, modular contracting, contract rights
relationships.how_encoded: Procurement leverage and modular competition are multiplied by 1 - s*(1 - talent).

relationships.framework_row: Open source + maintenance funding
relationships.how_encoded: Open source's portability effect is multiplied by 1 - s*(1 - maintenance intensity).

relationships.framework_row: Open source + data rights + open APIs
relationships.how_encoded: Extra portability growth of s * open_source * portability.

relationships.framework_row: Digital team + legal mandate + continuous funding (durability)
relationships.how_encoded: Stable funding cuts staff attrition by s * funding intensity.

relationships.framework_row: Digital team + legal mandate + continuous funding (durability)
relationships.how_encoded: Adds s * mandate intensity to every lever's protection against a hostile successor.

relationships.framework_row: Digital team + legal mandate + continuous funding (durability)
relationships.how_encoded: Adds s * funding stability to every lever's protection against a hostile successor.

relationships.framework_row: Success criterion 'durable': who would defend it?
relationships.how_encoded: Adds s * public legitimacy to every lever's protection against a hostile successor.

relationships.framework_row: Policy simplification -> any delivery strategy
relationships.how_encoded: Quality and reach gains are multiplied by 1 - s*(1 - policy fit).

relationships.framework_row: Constraint 1 (market power): vendors control the systems needed to change services
relationships.how_encoded: Quality and reach gains are multiplied by 1 - s * lock-in, so reducing lock-in raises the return to other levers.

relationships.framework_row: Shared platforms + central authority + funding
relationships.how_encoded: Platform growth is multiplied by 1 + s * authority intensity.

relationships.framework_row: Shared platforms + central authority + funding
relationships.how_encoded: Platform growth is multiplied by 1 + s * funding intensity.

relationships.framework_row: Startup pipeline + portability
relationships.how_encoded: New-entrant competition is multiplied by 1 - s*(1 - portability).

relationships.framework_row: Startup pipeline vs. public option
relationships.how_encoded: New-entrant competition is multiplied by 1 - s * public option intensity.

relationships.framework_row: Spend controls vs. agency autonomy for product teams
relationships.how_encoded: Talent's contribution to quality is multiplied by 1 - s * authority intensity.

relationships.framework_row: Cooperative purchasing vs. modular contracting
relationships.how_encoded: Modular procurement's competition effect is multiplied by 1 - s * collaboration intensity.

relationships.framework_row: In-house capacity: pace (moving work in-house needs experienced staff to manage migration)
relationships.how_encoded: The speed at which work can move in-house is multiplied by 1 - s*(1 - talent).

relationships.framework_row: In-house capacity: scale (hiring reform and a credible core team speed recruitment)
relationships.how_encoded: The maximum hiring rate is multiplied by 1 + s * team intensity.

relationships.framework_row: In-house capacity: scope (pooled teams and shared platforms let small jurisdictions run more)
relationships.how_encoded: The insourcing ceiling rises by s * collaboration intensity + s * shared infrastructure.

relationships.framework_row: AI shock: whether AI strengthens the state or the vendor depends on how it is built or procured
relationships.how_encoded: Share of AI capability absorbed by public capacity = s * (weighted talent, portability, shared infrastructure, insourced share); the rest arrives through vendors and deepens dependency.

relationships.framework_row: AI shock: large, fast AI procurement deepens dependency unless contracts are unbundled
relationships.how_encoded: AI-driven lock-in growth is multiplied by 1 - s * procurement intensity * talent gate.

relationships.framework_row: AI shock: errors and opaque automated decisions erode trust
relationships.how_encoded: The AI hit to legitimacy is multiplied by 1 - s * safeguards intensity.

relationships.framework_row: Success criterion 'scalable': pooled capacity for small jurisdictions
relationships.how_encoded: Cuts the cost of shareable levers (team, insourcing, open source, maintenance, platforms) by s.

effort_reasons.team: Recruiting, paying, and keeping skilled staff.
effort_reasons.insourcing: Years of hiring and migrating work off vendor systems.
effort_reasons.authority: Setting up a central office and getting agencies to follow it.
effort_reasons.mandate: Legislation: building a majority and a coalition, often over more than one session.
effort_reasons.funding: Winning a stable budget line, and defending it every year.
effort_reasons.policy: Reviewing and rewriting rules, often with lawyers and policy staff.
effort_reasons.procurement: Redesigning contracts and building the skills to manage them.
effort_reasons.portability: Contract negotiation with entrenched vendors: often waits for renewal and can mean legal disputes.
effort_reasons.entrants: Running marketplaces and challenges, and supporting new vendors.
effort_reasons.open_source: Changing how code is bought, written, and published.
effort_reasons.maintenance: Mostly a steady budget line for upkeep.
effort_reasons.platforms: Building and running shared services many agencies depend on.
effort_reasons.collaboration: Agreeing on shared governance and budgets with other governments.
effort_reasons.safeguards: Registers, assessments, accessibility work, and ways to appeal.
effort_reasons.public_option: Building and running the whole service yourself.
